 Oral Judgment

1. The claimants being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation of Rs.10,46,000/- awarded by the Tribunal are in appeal seeking enhancement, whereas the insurer is in appeal challenging the quantum of compensation on the ground that the same is excessive.

2. It is not in dispute that as a result of the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 18.12.2015,
Nanjundaswamy, a 24 year old died.

3. It is not in dispute that the Insurer is liable to pay the compensation as the offending vehicle was insured.
4.

The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence adduced before it, has come to the conclusion that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for the accident which has resulted in the death of Nanjundasamy.

The Tribunal has thereafter NC: 2024:KHC:51094 proceeded to award the following sums as compensation:
Compensation Sl. awarded by the Nature of Heads No. Tribunal (In Rs.)
1. Loss of Dependency 9,36,000/-
Transportation of dead body 2. 25,000/-
and miscellaneous charges 3. Loss of love and affection 50,000/-
4. Loss of estate 10,000/-
Funeral and obsequies 5. 25,000/-
expenses Total : 10,46,000/-
5.
In order to arrive at the loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income of the deceased notionally at Rs.6,500/- as there was no proof of his actual income.

sentences.text: In cases where there is no evidence to determine the actual income, it is appropriate to adopt the notional income as assessed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which for the accidents of the year 2015 would be Rs.9,000/-.

As per the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi1, as the deceased was aged about 24 years, 40% of the same (Rs.3,600/-) is required to be added to the said income as future prospects and the resultant income would be Rs.12,600/-.
8. Since the deceased was survived by his parents, out of the said sum, 1/3rd (Rs.4,200/-) would have to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
The net income will be Rs.8,400/-.
9. As the deceased was aged 24 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma2, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.

10. Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.18,14,400/- (Rs.8,400/- x 12 x '18')
towards "loss of dependency".
National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others - (2017) 16 SCC 680 Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2024:KHC:51094 11.

12.

16. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursal in terms of the award.
